Summary of the real-time leak detection scenarios., Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t127 container abstracts\n\t\t\t\t\t128 container abs0001\n\t\t\t\t\t\t129 heading Highlights, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t130 text Highlights\n\t\t\t\t\t\t131 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t132 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t133 text •\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t134 container para0001\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t135 text A semi-supervised approach for \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t136 link Description: leak detection, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t137 text  and localization (LD&L) is presented.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t138 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t139 text •\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t140 text The approach is based on conditional, convolutional generative adversarial networks.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t141 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t142 text •\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t143 text The model is trained for image-to-image translation of demand to pressure distributions.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t144 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t145 text •\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t146 container para0004\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t147 text The structural \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t148 link Description: similarity index, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t149 text  is employed to identify anomalies.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t150 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t151 text •\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t152 text This method is well-suited for real-time applications due to the low computational cost.\n\t\t\t\t\t153 container abs0002\n\t\t\t\t\t\t154 heading Abstract, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t155 text Abstract\n\t\t\t\t\t\t156 container spara020\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t157 text This paper explores the use of ‘\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t158 text conditional convolutional generative adversarial networks\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t159 text ’ (CDCGAN) for image-based leak detection and localization (LD&L) in water distribution networks (WDNs). The method employs pressure measurements and is based on four pillars: (1) hydraulic model-based generation of leak-free training data by taking into account the demand uncertainty, (2) conversion of hydraulic model input demand-output pressure pairs into images using kriging interpolation, (3) training of a CDCGAN model for image-to-image translation, and (4) using the structural similarity (SSIM) index for LD&L. SSIM, computed over the entire pressure distribution image is used for leak detection, and a local estimate of SSIM is employed for leak localization. The CDCGAN model employed in this paper is based on the pix2pix architecture. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is demonstrated on leakage datasets under various scenarios. Results show that the method has an accuracy of approximately 70% for real-time leak detection. The proposed method is well-suited for real-time applications due to the low computational cost of CDCGAN predictions compared to WDN hydraulic models, is robust in presence of uncertainty due to the nature of generative adversarial networks, and scales well to large and variable-sized monitoring data due to the use of an image-based approach.\n\t\t\t\t\t160 container abs0003\n\t\t\t\t\t\t161 heading Graphical abstract, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t162 text Graphical abstract\n\t\t\t\t\t\t163 container fig0017\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t164 image Image, graphical abstract\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t165 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t166 link Description: Download: Download high-res image (216KB), Help: Download high-res image (216KB), Value: ars.els-cdn.com/con…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t167 link Description: Download: Download full-size image, Help: Download full-size image, Value: ars.els-cdn.com/con…\n\t\t\t\t168 container keys0001\n\t\t\t\t\t169 heading Keywords, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t170 text Keywords\n\t\t\t\t\t171 text Leak\n\t\t\t\t\t172 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t173 text Anomaly detection\n\t\t\t\t\t174 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t175 text Generative adversarial networks\n\t\t\t\t\t176 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t177 text Image-to-image translation\n\t\t\t\t\t178 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t179 text Structural similarity index\n\t\t\t\t\t180 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t181 text Water Distribution\n\t\t\t\t182 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t183 link Description: Previous article in this issue, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t184 link Description: Next article in this issue, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t185 container body\n\t\t\t\t\t186 container sec0001\n\t\t\t\t\t\t187 heading 1. Introduction, Value: 2, ID: cesectitle0006\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t188 text 1 .  Introduction\n\t\t\t\t\t\t189 container para0007\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t190 text With the rapid development of supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) technologies, real-time monitoring of \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t191 link Description: hydraulic parameters, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t192 text  is becoming increasingly commonplace in many water \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t193 link Description: distribution networks, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t194 text  (WDNs) (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t195 link Description: Zhou et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t196 text ). Monitoring is often performed by installing pressure and flow sensors in the transmission mains, allowing for an improved understanding of system behavior, and diagnosis of anomalous events, the most notable of which is pipe leaks. In this context, diagnosis of leakage often includes at least two aspects: (a) ‘leakage detection’, which is to detect if leakage has occurred, and usually ends with binary results (i.e. leak alarm on or off), or fuzzy values and probabilities between 0 and 1 to represent the likelihood of a leakage event in the system (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t197 link Description: Mounce et al., 2010, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t198 text ). (b) ‘Leak localization’ (or isolation) is the process of narrowing down the potential location of a leak to a specific area or district. The latter is a precursor to finding the leaky pipe(s) and then pinpointing the exact leakage location (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t199 link Description: Al Qahtani et al., 2020, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t200 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t201 container sec0002\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t202 heading 1.1. Literature review, Value: 3, ID: cesectitle0007\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t203 text 1.1 .  Literature review\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t204 container para0008\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t205 text Several past studies (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t206 link Description: Kang et al. 2017, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t207 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t208 link Description: Guo et al. 2021, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t209 text ) rely on \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t210 link Description: auxiliary, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t211 text  data such as acoustic and vibration signals, for more accurate LD&L in presence of nuisance factors. Despite the effectiveness, obtaining such data is labor intensive, and the quality of these data can be affected by background noise and other events in the system or its environment (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t212 link Description: Wu and Liu, 2017, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t213 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t214 container para0009\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t215 text Leakages in pipeline systems can also be detected using transient analysis by relying on the principle of \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t216 link Description: pressure transient, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t217 text  wave reflection. A comprehensive overview of these methods was provided by \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t218 link Description: Abdulshaheed et al. (2017), Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t219 text . However, the effectiveness of transient analysis-based detection techniques is heavily influenced by pipe characteristics and external factors (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t220 link Description: Kammoun et al., 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t221 text ). Furthermore, this approach is unsuitable for detecting leaks over long pipe distances since pressure waves only propagate short distances. Additionally, implementing this technique often requires intricate mathematical algorithms and substantial computational resources (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t222 link Description: Wan et al., 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t223 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t224 container para0010\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t225 text Pressure and flow sensors have the advantage of being easy to install, enabling real-time monitoring, and being sensitive to leakage events. Therefore, leakage detection and localization (LD&L) using pressure/flow data has received increasing attention in the past decades. LD&L using pressure/flow data can be done through one of the following two groups of methods. The distinguishing factor between the two is whether a \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t226 link Description: hydraulic model, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t227 text  is used or not (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t228 link Description: Wan et al., 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t229 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t230 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t231 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t232 text A\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t233 container para0011\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t234 text ‘Data-driven’ methods rely on historical \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t235 link Description: monitoring data, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t236 text  and involve spatial analysis of changes across a WDN, or temporal pattern analysis of time series data. Methods in this group may involve: (1) defining control limits by calculating some statistical characteristic (e.g. exponentially weighted moving average) of historical measurements and defining data that is outside these limits as potential leaks (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t237 link Description: Jung et al. 2015, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t238 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t239 link Description: Loureiro et al. 2016, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t240 text ). These methods often rely on assumptions such as the \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t241 link Description: Gaussianity, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t242 text  of data distribution and the \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t243 link Description: uncorrelation, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t244 text  of errors. (2) Using \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t245 link Description: historical data, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t246 text  to train a predictor model that learns the expected behavior of the system in leak-free circumstances, and comparing the residuals between the observed and predicted value with a threshold to identify leaks. A variety of machine learning tools, such as \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t247 link Description: support vector machines, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t248 text  and classic \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t249 link Description: neural networks, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t250 text  have been employed in this context (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t251 link Description: Mounce et al. 2011, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t252 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t253 link Description: Romano et al. 2012, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t254 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t255 link Description: Tijani et al. 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t256 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t257 link Description: Tariq et al. 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t258 text ). (3) Reframing the spatial/temporal pattern recognition as a classification problem (using e.g. Bayesian classifiers) (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t259 link Description: Wu et al. 2016, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t260 text ). This method requires labeled data, i.e. an indication of whether a chosen data instance pertains to a leak or not. (4) Formulating LD&L as a \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t261 link Description: clustering problem, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t262 text  by grouping similar data into different clusters, and identifying leaks as those that are dissimilar to normal cluster(s) (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t263 link Description: Wu and Liu 2020, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t264 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t265 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t266 text B\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t267 container para0012\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t268 text ‘Model-based’ methods, also known as physically-based or process-based methods, rely on the comparison of measured data with those of a calibrated WDN hydraulic model. Model-based methods include: (1) formulating LD&L as an inverse modeling problem using an optimization algorithm, and one or multiple objective function(s) (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t269 link Description: Sanz et al. 2016, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t270 text ). (2) Relying on sensitivity-to-leak analysis (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t271 link Description: Perez et al. 2014, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t272 text ), where model-generated pressure disturbances caused by all possible \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t273 link Description: leak locations, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t274 text  and magnitudes are stored in a leak-sensitivity matrix and matched against the difference between measured and simulated data (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t275 link Description: Soldevila et al., 2017, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t276 text ). (3) Generating pressure or \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t277 link Description: pressure residual, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t278 text  maps of each leakage scenario using the hydraulic model, employing the resulting data to train a classifier, and finally utilizing the trained classifier for LD&L. The latter is sometimes referred to as a mixed model-based/data-driven approach (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t279 link Description: Soldevila et al., 2016, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t280 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t281 container para0013\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t282 text Both data-driven and model-based methods have their advantages and limitations, and it is unfeasible to draw a conclusion about which method is universally superior (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t283 link Description: Wan et al., 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t284 text ). Data-driven approaches directly incorporate experimental data, and hence don't require a deep knowledge of the system operation and physical equations. Data-driven methods are best suited for WDNs with a long-term monitoring dataset and were found to be effective in leak detection. However, their performance in leak localization is debated (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t285 link Description: Wu and Liu, 2017, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t286 text ). It is generally difficult to obtain enough correct labeled data to train a high-accuracy model in a supervised manner (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t287 link Description: Zhang et al., 2020, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t288 text ); therefore data-driven LD&L methods often rely on unsupervised or semi-supervised training. Many commonly used tools within the context of the data-driven approach have limitations in learning complex features and using them requires the manual design of suitable feature extractors (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t289 link Description: Zhou et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t290 text ). Data-driven methods are particularly vulnerable to missing or faulty data (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t291 link Description: Hu et al., 2021, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t292 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t293 container para0014\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t294 text Model-based methods are preferred when limited historical data is available, but come at the cost of building and calibrating a hydraulic model. Moreover, the high computation demand of hydraulic models often hinders achieving real-time LD&L. A common challenge for both model-based and data-driven methods is that pressure and flow rate can be affected by other factors apart from leakages, such as variability and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t295 link Description: stochasticity, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t296 text  in demand and \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t297 link Description: random errors, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t298 text  in sensor measurements. These are often difficult to distinguish from leaks. For model-based methods, the effect of input parameter uncertainty on the model output flow and pressure, adds to this complexity (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t299 link Description: Menapace et al., 2018, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t300 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t301 link Description: Sun et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t302 text ). Hence model-based methods do not perform well in larger WDNs where the models' output uncertainty is often higher compared to smaller WDNs (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t303 link Description: Zhou et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t304 text ). The performance of the model-based sensitivity-to-leak analysis method is particularly well-known to decrease due to the nodal demand uncertainty and noise in the measurements (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t305 link Description: Cugueró-Escofet et al., 2015, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t306 text ).\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t307 container para0015\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t308 text The above-described challenges have forced previous LD&L studies to focus mainly on hypothetical burst events in simple WDNs (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t309 link Description: Wan et al., 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t310 text ). As highlighted by recent review papers (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t311 link Description: Gupta and Kulat 2018, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t312 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t313 link Description: Chan et al. 2018, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t314 text , \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t315 link Description: Wan et al. 2022, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t316 text ), more effort is needed to solve these challenges by developing novel methods that are: (a) robust in presence of various forms of uncertainty, (b) can scale to very large monitoring datasets, (c) can learn complex features from raw data, (d) rely less on manual design, and (e) are well-adapted to a limitation in labeled training data.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t317 container para0016\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t318 text A promising approach to achieve this objective is to exploit \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t319 link Description: deep neural networks, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t320 text  (DNNs). DNNs rely on hierarchical projections of the input space into increasingly low-dimensional latent representations (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t321 link Description: Goodfellow et al., 2016, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t322 text ), enabling them to learn complex features from large amounts of data without the need for developing manual features by domain experts (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t323 link Description: Chalapathy and Chawla, 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t324 text ). In recent years, several DNN-based \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t325 link Description: anomaly detection, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t326 text  methods have been introduced for a variety of applications, demonstrating significantly better performance than conventional anomaly detection with an increase in the scale of data and complexity of the problem (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t327 link Description: Pang et al., 2021, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t328 text ). Example applications of DNNs in LD&L include the use of \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t329 link Description: convolutional neural networks, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t330 text  (CNNs) for burst localization based on data from short-duration pressure observations (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t331 link Description: Zhou et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t332 text ); supervised training of a CNN using hydraulic model-generated samples of all possible leaks for leak localization (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t333 link Description: Javadiha et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t334 text ). These approaches, like many older methods, require a well-calibrated hydraulic model to generate synthetic data that accurately represent real-life situations for training a \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t335 link Description: deep learning, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t336 text  model. However, acquiring and maintaining a well-calibrated hydraulic model can be challenging for water companies.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t337 container para0017\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t338 text Regression analysis has been used as an alternative method to learn the data patterns representing the healthy state of a WDN from historical monitoring data instead of a hydraulic model. As an example, \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t339 link Description: Ye and Fenner (2011), Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t340 text  utilized the \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t341 link Description: Kalman filter, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t342 text  to fit historical \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t343 link Description: flow measurements, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t344 text  and identify burst events by comparing predicted and observed values, while also employing the weighted \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t345 link Description: least squares, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t346 text  regression to model the data. However, these approaches treat each data point of a day independently, and thus, they do not fully consider the \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t347 link Description: autocorrelation, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t348 text  of the time series data.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t349 container para0018\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t350 link Description: Mounce et al. (2010), Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t351 text  employed a neural network to learn the normal flow behavior from monitoring data and detect leaks based on prediction errors. A key limitation of their approach is the inability to share features across different steps of a time series, whereas temporal pattern recognition requires the ability to process evolving patterns. To address this problem, \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t352 link Description: recurrent neural networks, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t353 text  such as long short-term memory (LSTM) networks have been explored for leakage detection (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t354 link Description: Wang et al., 2020, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t355 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t356 link Description: Xu et al., 2020, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t357 text ). While the results of these LSTM-based methods have shown high detection accuracy, there are still some limitations that need to be addressed. Specifically, these methods are often restricted to univariate time series analysis, which only allows for the analysis of data from a single sensor at a time. However, it's known that data from sensors in the same network are spatially correlated, and considering topology information and the spatial relation of the sensors is essential for accurate leak detection.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t358 container sec0003\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t359 heading 1.2. Study objectives, Value: 3, ID: cesectitle0008\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t360 text 1.2 .  Study objectives\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t361 container para0019\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t362 text Recent research progress has demonstrated the effectiveness of DNNs in solving LD&L problems, and it is becoming increasingly clear that DNNs present an opportunity for improving current practice. In this work, we will be leveraging some of the most recent advances in DNNs, to develop a robust methodology for achieving accurate real-time LD&L in complex settings. Our methodology is based on the use of ‘\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t363 text conditional convolutional generative adversarial networks\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t364 text ’ (CDCGAN) for image-based anomaly detection. Partially similar methods have been used in other applications for anomaly detection (e.g. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t365 link Description: Ezeme et al. 2020, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t366 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t367 link Description: Luo et al. 2021, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t368 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t369 link Description: Qiu et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t370 text ), but to the best of our knowledge, this method has not been applied to leak detection in WDNs.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t371 container para0020\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t372 text Relying on \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t373 link Description: flow measurements, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t374 text  for LD&L is often easier than pressure measurements, because flow data allows for the use of simple mass balance relations, and pressure data is less sensitive to leak events, especially when the pressure sensor is located far from the leak location (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t375 link Description: Ye and Fenner, 2011, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t376 text ). However, pressure meters are easier to install and less costly than \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t377 link Description: flow meters, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t378 text  (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t379 link Description: Zhou et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t380 text ; \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t381 link Description: Sun et al., 2019, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t382 text ), provide instantaneous data, and are better for LD&L in WDNs where there is a dense mesh of pipes with only flow measurements at the entrance of each \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t383 link Description: DMA, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t384 text  (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t385 link Description: Soldevila et al., 2017, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t386 text ). Hence, this work focuses on the use of pressure data for LD&L.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t387 container para0021\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t388 text The rest of the paper is organized as follows. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t389 link Description: Section 2, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t390 text  presents the background of semi-supervised anomaly detection (SSAD) and CDCGANs. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t391 link Description: Section 3, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t392 text  presents the proposed methodology for LD&L. \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t393 link Description: Section 4, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t394 text  details the application of the method to a WDN, followed by a discussion of the main findings. Finally, \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t395 link Description: Section 5, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t396 text  draws the main conclusions of the work and introduces some potential extensions.\n\t\t\t\t\t397 container sec0004\n\t\t\t\t\t\t398 heading 2. Theoretical background, Value: 2, ID: cesectitle0009\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t399 text .  Theoretical background\n\t\t\t\t\t\t400 container sec0005\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t401 heading 2.1. Semi-supervised deep anomaly detection, Value: 3, ID: cesectitle0010\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t402 text 2.1 .  Semi-supervised deep anomaly detection\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t403 container para0022\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t404 text Leaks result in anomalous pressure observations, and most notably, a contextual anomaly. Therefore, LD&L in \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t405 link Description: WDNs, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t406 text  can be described as a particular case of the general problem of \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t407 link Description: anomaly detection, Value: sciencedirect.com/t…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t408 text  and isolation in dynamic systems (\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t409 link Description: Soldevila et al., 2016, Value: sciencedirect.com/s…\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t410 text ).
